correctness.rationale: A complete proof establishes the exact open-neighborhood equivalence for cubic prisms, the transfer bijection for n>=3, the 84-state/384-edge graph, and the formal log-determinant identity. A fully included dependency-free integer checker computes all 84 power traces and Newton identities and verifies every coefficient of the factored degree-36 determinant. Separate direct graph coloring enumeration n=3,4,5 and the three-color n=3..6 agree, but are expressly not used as infinite proofs. Three-color forcing and three common-based 4-color cycles establish the minimum palette. Exact connectivity/aperiodicity checks plus polynomial eigenvalue bounds justify the asymptotics.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: A scalar chromatic-number theorem, a three-color homogeneous criterion, or a result for crossed/stacked prisms does not entail the explicit rational four-palette generating function, 84-state factored determinant, and enumeration/growth of every optimum partition on the complementary residue classes.

evidence: For cubic graphs, proper conflict-free open-neighborhood coloring is equivalent to proper 2-dynamic coloring because three equal neighbor colors is the only forbidden multiplicity pattern.
Madaras and Šurimová, Homogeneous colourings of graphs, DOI 10.21136/MB.2022.0007-21, Theorem 3: three-color homogeneous prism patterns force circumference divisible by three.
Fabrici et al., arXiv:2202.02570, full HTML, Sec. 1: formal proper conflict-free open-neighborhood definition.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The recognized dynamic/homogeneous terminologies were searched rather than treating a name difference as originality. The existing three-color phase is credited. A proper 4-palette coloring can have vertices seeing 2 or 3 neighbor colors, so homogeneous coloring classifications do not imply the count of all dynamic four-palette colorings. No matching spectrum or rational series emerged.

evidence: The new direct graph count is 264,384,3600 for circumferences 3,4,5; these are also coefficients of a separately certified degree-36 determinant rational series.
Searches for the numerical prefix, parameter aliases, and existing coloring polynomials returned no directly covering four-palette table.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: A finite known chromatic-number table or ordinary prism chromatic polynomial would not enumerate colorings with the additional local neighborhood restriction. Failed lookup is not a proof of novelty; completeness rests on the non-implication comparisons with closest source content, and unidentified exact tables remain a residual risk.

originality.rationale: The contribution assessed as new is the explicit full four-palette rational generating function and optimum-partition enumerator, not the known three-color period-three obstruction. Primary prior work defines proper conflict-free coloring, develops general bounds, and analyzes homogeneous prism color palettes without furnishing an exact four-palette census. No equivalent exact rational series or broader enumerative theorem was identified by multiple phrase, graph-alias, sequence and parameter searches. Priority overlap with unindexed or inaccessible full text is acknowledged.
residual_risks: Public full text of the 2022 homogeneous-coloring article was unavailable in the current session; the accessible theorem passage establishes the earlier three-color criterion but cannot exclude hidden enumerative appendix material.
Unindexed papers or alternate labels for periodic dynamic-coloring polynomials could contain the same four-palette generating function. Search absence is not a uniqueness theorem.

value.rationale: The primary output is an exact all-circumference rational counting series and explicit characteristic factorization, not merely a known small chromatic-number bound. It yields the full optimum partition count: exactly two in circumferences divisible by three, exponentially many with sharp base 5.0340418358... otherwise. Both the full enumeration and this arithmetic structural dichotomy are natural graph-coloring questions and are not determined by the earlier three-color obstruction.
